hub_title: Learn Jev — typed decisions for software
tagline: A general reference hub for TypeSafe AI's Jev: System One models, primitives, confidence gates, and how they sit beside LLM agents — not a one-day course site.
disclaimer: Personal learning and research packaging only. Unofficial; not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by TypeSafe AI or any organization named here. Not legal, financial, or professional advice. Vendor speed/cost claims are reported as published — verify on your workload. See DISCLAIMER.md.
audience: Practitioners and architects who want a clean map of Jev / System One: concepts, sources, decks, and related Almeida (RLHF → automation) context.

overview.blurb: Jev is TypeSafe AI's flagship System One model: program state in, typed probabilistic decisions out (Choice, Score, Noul). This hub packages two presentation decks, six ~30s shorts, long-form video/audio, visuals, a full NotebookLM NEXUS library, and a Sources ledger — plus reframed study notes without a day timer.

topics.title: What Jev is
topics.body: System One model class: fast structured decisions for software. Flagship model jev-latest. Named after Jevons (cheaper intelligence → more demand), not a chatbot.

topics.title: Three primitives
topics.body: Choice (labelled options), Score (ordered levels), Noul (yes/no probability). Many questions, one state, one round trip.

topics.title: When not to use it
topics.body: Open-ended writing, planning prose, tool-call narration, or tiny Choice sets forced onto unbounded problems. Keep an LLM (or human) for language; escalate on low confidence.

topics.title: Related thesis
topics.body: Almeida's assistance vs automation framing (RLHF optimizes for human preference) motivates automation-native decision models — Jev / RLCD is the product bet, still early-access.

visuals.title: Jev = typed decisions, not chat
visuals.caption: State in → System One evaluation → Choice / Score / Noul with probabilities. Code branches; Jev does not write prose.

visuals.title: System One (Jev) vs LLM agent
visuals.caption: LLMs generate plans and replies. Jev answers closed questions your schema defines. Most agent loops need both.

visuals.title: Confidence gate
visuals.caption: Act when probability clears a threshold; otherwise escalate to a human or an LLM. Calibration is aggregate, not a warranty on one call.

visuals.title: Jev decision layer vs LLMs
visuals.caption: NotebookLM infographic: decision-layer framing versus generative LLM workflows.
